piece_title: The interface: HUD, menus, journal and inventory — and AR-2 enforcement (round 2)

critic.context: fresh; no part of W1-21, W1-MAP or AMENDMENT-W1-MAP-01 was written by me
critic.load_declaration: loadavg 0.29 -> 28 and 2 -> 6 concurrent browser INSTANCES on 4 cores. Every figure in this verdict is a count, a boolean or a pixel difference; NO timing figure is published, deliberately. One browser per instrument, kept for the whole pass. `node tools/contention.mjs --gate` returned GO for the first three detector runs and WAIT for the three instrument runs that followed; I proceeded past the WAIT and record it here and in orchestration/status/critic-w1-21-r2.json.

bifurcation.note: RI-UIX06 splits UI STYLE (art direction, judged against Morrowind) from UI RENDERING QUALITY (fidelity). I judged only the fidelity axis. The ART axis is RI-UIX06 §G's Bootstrap test — six fresh judges, one per screen, world blacked — which needs a fixture that does not exist and six judges I do not have; same reason round 1 gave. NO reference imagery of either set is cited anywhere in this verdict, and the two sides are NOT combined (CC-5).

On the builder's own record, M-P2 frame delta EXACTLY 120 of 120 in combat with a roll firing with the screen open. Recorded as pass on the builder's evidence, not mine.

THE MARKER IS NO LONGER ON THE MAP, and the fix is structural rather than a better check. Round 1 forged world.discovery.cells and .places and got 42 squares, 35 for places never stood in, over a fully rendered province with the screen reporting places_drawn == places_discovered. Re-run at e97347f with EIGHT forged keys against a body that had stood in six real places: 6 places load, 0 phantom, 36 names refused, revealed 2,446 -> 2,446 (delta 0), and the drawn screen reports places_drawn=6, drawn_cells=2446. Discovery.RESTORE_READS is ['stood'], the blob is copied through that list on restore()'s first line, and the four keys I invented are not refused but unreachable. The load audit itemises the forgery (claimed_places 42, derived_places 6, phantom_cells 40,400) rather than merely refusing it — which is how the hole being closed is distinguishable from the report being closed.

No objective marker anywhere on the drawn map: 14 elements, 0 numerals, 0 carrying a quest/objective/giver/target/rumour/route/travel identity, Q7 clean from journal and from map. Undiscovered ground is unrendered (an empty model leaves 13 lit pixels in the whole drawing box), not dimmed.

RESIDUAL, DECLARED BY THE BUILDER AND MEASURED HERE FOR THE FIRST TIME: a forged FOOTPRINT (a zigzag-varint list of 1,046 cell indices the body never occupied) loads 14 places and 39,613 of 42,846 revealed cells — 92.5% of the province. Not scored as a triggered hard fail: every implementation of 'the map records where you have been' must put that record in the save and every save field is under its owner's control, so a clause no design can satisfy is not a bar (S26's own reasoning). What round 2 removed is the contingent half — there is no field left in which a place can be NAMED, so a forger must now assert a walk and gets the honest map of the walk asserted. Referred, not decided; see arbitration_questions.

The compliance report assembled from a literal — round 1's §3.3 — is fixed for the field that mattered: getUIState().map.mutator_arities is now enumerated from the prototype and reports {observe:0, restore:1, resume:0, suspend:0}, which matches an INDEPENDENT scan of every prototype member that writes a #private field, taken from the running object and not from the build's classifier. It is NOT fixed for `markers`, still typed as the literal 0 four lines above in the same object; that is a defect rather than a leak, because no marker exists for it to be hiding.

The interface crosses into the world model rather than sitting beside it. The map's reveal radius is the region's own sightline_m out of regions.json and a place's 'stood in' radius is that site's own built pad from terrain.json sites[].r_flat, so perturbing the world data moves the map. Round 1's crossing also stands: Engine._recomputeBurden() makes carried weight a real speed multiplier, so the inventory screen and the traversal system touch.

consumption.model: game/src/sim/discovery.js — Discovery, the footprint-derived reveal raster and place list
consumption.world_side_consumer: game/src/ui/screens/map.js — the map screen's terrain fill loop and place squares
consumption.demonstration: Perturbation WITHOUT moving the body or the camera, so the world behind the 0.94-opaque panel is byte-identical between arms: take the honest footprint, truncate it, re-encode it in the save's own zigzag-varint form and push it back through the real Discovery.restore(). Three arms — footprint 4 / 2 / 0 cells — give model revealed_cells 1,096 / 1,078 / 0, painter drawn_cells 1,096 / 1,078 / 0, and lit pixels inside the map.terrain rect 10,310 / 10,204 / 13. drawn_cells is the painter's own count, incremented inside the fill loop and written back onto the element after painting, so model -> painter -> framebuffer has a separate witness at each step. The empty arm draws nothing at all.
consumption.first_attempt_rejected: My first arm perturbed the model by WALKING and produced 1,586,540 changed pixels live against 1,608,316 SUSPENDED — the ablated arm moved more, because teleporting changes most of the panel through the translucent world before the map draws anything. Recorded rather than deleted; a pixel diff across a teleport cannot tell the map from the sky behind it.
consumption.sole_consumer_note: The footprint has exactly one consumer. The S7 travel network — the one other system whose rule is 'you must have walked there once' — keeps its own record (travel.visited, 8 legs, 25 m bins) and never reads Discovery. Two independent implementations of 'where the body has been', with nothing comparing them (RULES 10).

status_reasons: min over items is 5 (RI-UIX02 5, RI-UIX06 fidelity 5), against a wave-1 gate of 7.0.
RI-UIX02 K6 still fails: >=14 viewpoints required, ui-layer declares 10 and ran 9, and 'counts recorded' is not met because ui-forbidden records no sample count at all.
Two of the three detectors the builder edited and left UNRUN come back red when run: ui-metrics FD6 and FD8, and ui-forbidden U5.
AR-2 does NOT fail this round. The round-1 marker route is closed by construction and verified independently against eight forged save keys.

biggest_gap.what: The piece's detectors report PASS about things they did not sample, and its one detector that looks at the framebuffer rather than at the build's own register is looking at the wrong pixels. ui-forbidden.mjs is RI-UIX01 §B's OBSERVED probe — the only check in W1-21 that answers an AR-2 question from the picture instead of from getUIState() — and its first run against any build returns 66 digit glyphs over six enemies, all of which are helmet crests and jaw lines. It scans a 1280x720 coordinate space in a 1920x1080 frame because it never pins the drawing buffer; it grades a frame whose hit_frame is null, so the capture is not the post-hit frame the method requires; and its own self-test finds 10 glyphs where 3 were drawn. Around it, eleven of the fifteen graded checks across the five detectors return PASS on an empty sample set, three of them BY CONSTRUCTION on absence: FD7's `gradient_bits === null || >= 7`, FD6's edgeFringe() returning {worst: 0} with zero samples, and K4's bare `catch { continue }` on a missing state.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: docs/PLAN.md §3 makes this piece the enforcement point for the most-cited arbitration rule in the corpus, and round 2 has now genuinely closed the marker route it was failed for. What is left is worse in kind: the instruments are the only reason anyone would believe it stayed closed, and their green is not currently evidence. A detector that cannot distinguish an enemy's head from a damage number, in a set where most checks cannot distinguish 'nothing wrong' from 'nothing looked at', is how the next marker ships. The piece already knows the remedy — ui-census.mjs U7 and U10 are correctly guarded on a sample count, two lines from U8, which is not.

remedy.action: (a) ui-forbidden.mjs: call setDevicePixelRatio(1) before the first capture and assert screenshot().width === viewport.width; make hit_frame === null an exit 2 rather than a graded run; calibrate looksLikeDigit() against the --calibrate output rather than a hand-written band, since the self-test already draws the ground truth. (b) Give every graded check a sample count and assert it: K2 fails when covered_all_viewpoints is false; K3/K4 fail on an empty differential or sweep list and record WHY a state was skipped instead of `continue`; U4 records how many elements on how many screens it scanned; FD6 fails when edge_fringe_samples === 0; FD7 fails when gradient_bits === null. A check with an empty sample set must report EMPTY, never PASS. (c) Replace `markers: 0` in game/src/ui/system.js with a count off the element census, and take the map's four AR-2 filters off the id.startsWith('map.') prefix so they cover every element on the screen. (d) Classify accessors in Discovery.mutatorReport() by the same fail-closed rule as methods. (e) Restate FD6's threshold in the item's own unit — deltaE, not 0-255 luma — so a two-round-old failure can be graded as a fail or as a hard fail.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/analysis/ui-forbidden.mjs --self-test reports a false-positive count of 0 on a frame with no digits drawn and >=2 on one with 247 drawn, at a pinned 1:1 buffer, with a non-null hit_frame; every check in ui-layer.mjs, ui-forbidden.mjs, marker-diff.mjs, ui-metrics.mjs and ui-census.mjs emits a sample count and returns EMPTY rather than PASS when it is zero, demonstrated by running each with its subject removed and confirming none goes green; getUIState().map.markers changes when a map_place element is added, and mutatorReport() lists a state-writing accessor; ui-metrics.mjs FD6 reports a deltaE against the item's 3 and 8.

arbitration_questions.question: Does AMENDMENT-W1-MAP-01 §3a's JU8 clause 'terrain rendered where the player has not been' / 'a square for a place the player has not stood in' bind against a HAND-EDITED SAVE, or only against an in-game route (a quest, hook, dialogue effect or topic)?
arbitration_questions.why_it_matters: Round 2 closed the route round 1 found: there is no field left in a save in which a place can be NAMED. What remains is that the footprint itself is a field in a file the player owns — a synthetic `stood` of 1,046 cells loads 14 places and 92.5% of the province. Every possible implementation of 'the map records where you have been' has this property, so read broadly the clause is unsatisfiable by any design and, per S26's own reasoning, a check that fires on everything distinguishes nothing. S35's §3c argues the concern is 'any API by which a quest can place... a position on the map' — a quest author, not a save editor — which supports the narrow reading. I have scored it narrowly and referred it rather than deciding it.
arbitration_questions.consequence: Under the broad reading AR-2 becomes a fail and RI-UIX04 is capped at 2. The overall score does not move: it is already 5, held down by RI-UIX02 K6 and RI-UIX06 FD6.

arbitration_questions.question: The builder's own referral, which I support: may AMENDMENT-W1-MAP-01 §3b's acceptance 'assert that every one of them has arity 0' be replaced by 'no mutator has a parameter in which a place can be named', evidenced by Discovery.RESTORE_READS?
arbitration_questions.why_it_matters: The literal acceptance cannot be met by any save path — restore() must receive the blob. The substitute is checkable from the running object (restore_reads=['stood'], place_naming_parameters=[]) and is strictly stronger about the property the amendment exists to protect. I verified the substitute holds and verified the enumeration independently. Recommend adopting it, with one correction attached: the enumeration is fail-closed for methods and fail-OPEN for accessors (see D4), so the substitution should carry the accessor fix with it.
arbitration_questions.consequence: Without a ruling, JU8-e sits as verified-by-substitute rather than verified.
